chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from 'Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

For every prescribed salat there is a supererogatory prayer of two rak'ahs, except al-'Asr, for its nafilah is brought forward so that the two are before it, and they are the two rak'ahs by which the eight after al-Zuhr are completed. So when you want to make up something of the salat, prescribed or otherwise, then do not pray anything until you begin and pray before the obligatory prayer that has become due two rak'ahs as its nafilah; then make up whatever you wish. And begin in Salat al-Layl with the verses; you recite:
"Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth" up to "Indeed, You do not fail in the promise."

(1) "And on Friday you begin with the verses before the two rak'ahs that are before noon." And he said: "The time of Salat al-Jumu'ah is when the sun declines by a strap's width or half of it." And he said: "A man may pray the noon supererogatory prayer from the sun's decline until two feet have passed. So if from the noon prayer one rak'ah remains, or before two feet have passed, he completes the prayer until he prays the full rak'ahs. But if two feet have passed before he prays one rak'ah, he begins with the first obligatory prayer and does not pray the noon supererogatory prayer until after that. And a man may pray from the nawafil of the first prayer from the first prayer until four feet have passed. So if the four feet have passed and he has not prayed anything of the nawafil, then he does not pray the nawafil; but if he has prayed one rak'ah, then let him complete the nawafil until he finishes them, then he prays al-'Asr." And he said: "A man may pray, if something of the noon supererogatory prayer remains upon him, until after the coming of the first obligatory prayer by half a foot has passed; and if a man has prayed something of the nawafil of the first prayer before al-'Asr arrives, then he may complete the nawafil of the first prayer until after the coming of al-'Asr one foot has passed." And he said: "One foot after the arrival of al-'Asr is equal in time to half a foot after the arrival of the first prayer." And regarding a man who has many nights' prayers due upon him: is it permissible for him to make up many nights' prayers with their witrs, following one after another? He said: "Yes, that is allowed for him in the first part of the night. But once the night reaches its middle until dawn rises, it is not for a man or a woman to perform witr except the witr of that night's prayer. So if he wishes to make up a prayer due upon him, he prays eight rak'ahs from that night's prayer and delays the witr; then he makes up whatever seems fit to him without witr, then he performs the witr that belongs specifically to that night." And regarding a man who has a prayer due upon him from residence: may he make it up while he is traveling? He said: "Yes, he makes it up at night on the ground; but as for on the mount, no. And he prays as he prays while resident."

key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: the sun's decline from the meridian, marking the onset of noon prayer time
key_terms.الْوَتْرَ: the odd-unit concluding prayer of the night prayer
key_terms.صَلَاةِ اللَّيْلِ: the night prayer performed during the night
key_terms.مُسَافِرٌ: a traveler, in the context of prayer rulings during سفر
key_terms.نَافِلَةُ: a supererogatory prayer attached to an obligatory salat
key_terms.نَوَافِلِ: supererogatory prayers performed in addition to the obligatory salat

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings on the timing of nawafil, Salat al-Layl, and making up missed prayers in Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out rulings for the nawafil attached to the prescribed daily salat, their timing in relation to the obligatory prayers, and the order of making up missed prayers. It also addresses recitation in Salat al-Layl, special timing considerations on Friday, the rules of making up multiple night prayers with witr, and the manner of making up a resident's prayer while traveling.
